headline: World Bank ‘satisfied’ with $370m National Health Support Programme
summary: ISLAMABAD: The World Bank has rated the implementation progress of its $370 million National Health Support Programme (NHSP) in Punjab, Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as “satisfactory”, with a “moderate” overall risk rating, and expects the programme to meet its targets before the Dec 31, 2027 deadline.Effective since October 2022, the NHSP aims to advance universal health coverage by strengthening equitable access to and the quality of essential healthcare services at the primary level.The World Bank provided approximately $259m in financing, while the remaining funds came through grants and co-financing from the Global Financing Facility, the Gates Foundation, the Global Fund and Gavi.In its public disclosure, the Washington-based multilateral lender rated both, progress towards achieving the programme’s development objectives and overall implementation progress, as “satisfactory” while describing the overall risk as “moderate”.The NHSP “has sustained strong implementation momentum and continues to deliver tangible results across provinces”, the World Bank said, adding that approximately 76 per cent of total programme funding had been disbursed.Govt claims goods exports reached ‘all-time high’ of $11.4bn in July-October“Provincial governments have shown strong ownership, and the reforms introduced through the Disbursement Linked Results (DLRs) are strengthening primary health care systems. The remaining DLRs are on track, and all are expected to be achieved well ahead of the programme’s closing on Dec 31, 2027,” the bank noted.The World Bank has already disbursed $205m (79.3pc) of its $259m financing, while a $36.8m co-financing facility has been completely disbursed. Two other financing components of $35m and $29m have each recorded disbursements of 50pc, according to the lender.The programme uses a Program-for-Results (PforR) financing instrument, the first of its kind in Pakistan’s health sector, under which funding is linked to the achievement of agreed results.The approach builds on Pakistan’s universal health coverage reforms and improvements in implementation capacity demonstrated through the earlier National Immunisation Support Project, which included the federal health ministry and provincial governments.According to the World Bank, the programme’s improved health facility readiness score has reached 75pc in KP, 80pc in Punjab and 77.5pc in Sindh.However, the use of modern contraceptives among women of reproductive age remains relatively low at 15pc in KP, 30pc in Punjab and 20pc in Sindh.The NHSP complements existing investments in human capital and builds on reforms aimed at improving the quality of and equitable access to healthcare services.It focuses on three areas, including coverage and quality of essential healthcare services, governance and accountability and healthcare financing.Under the first component, the programme seeks to improve the availability of healthcare staff, supplies and essential medicines, while strengthening patient referral systems for emergency and higher-level care.Goods exports hit $11.4bnSeparately, the federal government said the country’s goods exports had reached “an all-time high” of $11.4bn during July-October of the current fiscal year, registering year-on-year growth of 8.8pc from $10.4bn in the corresponding period last year, the state-run Associated Press of Pakistan reported.In a statement, the government attributed the performance to measures introduced in the federal budget and coordinated efforts by the finance team and relevant institutions.Published in Dawn, November 16th, 2026

Two other financing components of $35m and $29m have each recorded disbursements of 50pc, according to the lender.The programme uses a Program-for-Results (PforR) financing instrument, the first of its kind in Pakistan’s health sector, under which funding is linked to the achievement of agreed results.The approach builds on Pakistan’s universal health coverage reforms and improvements in implementation capacity demonstrated through the earlier National Immunisation Support Project, which included the federal health ministry and provincial governments.According to the World Bank, the programme’s improved health facility readiness score has reached 75pc in KP, 80pc in Punjab and 77.5pc in Sindh.However, the use of modern contraceptives among women of reproductive age remains relatively low at 15pc in KP, 30pc in Punjab and 20pc in Sindh.The NHSP complements existing investments in human capital and builds on reforms aimed at improving the quality of and equitable access to healthcare services.It focuses on three areas, including coverage and quality of essential healthcare services, governance and accountability and healthcare financing.Under the first component, the programme seeks to improve the availability of healthcare staff, supplies and essential medicines, while strengthening patient referral systems for emergency and higher-level care.Goods exports hit $11.4bnSeparately, the federal government said the country’s goods exports had reached “an all-time high” of $11.4bn during July-October of the current fiscal year, registering year-on-year growth of 8.8pc from $10.4bn in the corresponding period last year, the state-run Associated Press of Pakistan reported.In a statement, the government attributed the performance to measures introduced in the federal budget and coordinated efforts by the finance team and relevant institutions.Published in Dawn, November 16th, 2026

headline: Islamabad hosts foreign dignitaries for two-day ECO ministerial meeting
summary: Foreign dignitaries arrived in Islamabad on Sunday as Pakistan hosts the two-day 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers,starting today.Currently, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Tajikistan, Iran, Turkiye, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyz Republic and Uzbekistan arepartof the ECO.Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar hosted a welcome dinner in honour of the foreign ministers and heads of delegations of the member states in Islamabad ahead of the meeting, the Foreign Office (FO) said on social media.He warmly welcomed the delegates and wished them productive deliberations while highlighting the close bonds among ECO member states, the FO said.Addressing the gathering, DPM Dar also reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to “regional cooperation and advancing shared aspirations for peace, progress and prosperity”.Alongside the visiting delegations, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Parliamentary Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhary, representatives of the ECO secretariat, members of the diplomatic corps, and senior officials of the foreign ministry were also in attendance, FO added.Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Deputy Secretary General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda, Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, Turkish Deputy Foreign Minister Musa Kulaklikaya, and Kyrgyz Republic’s Deputy FM Kairat Erkinovich Tursunkulov are among those in Islamabad for the meeting.Azeri Deputy FM Elnur Mammadov, Kazakh Deputy FM Arman Issagaliyev, and Turkmenistan’s FM Rashid Meredov also arrived in the federal capital today.At night, Iran’s FM Abbas Araghchi also landed in Islamabad for the moot, Iran’s state media reported.Upon his arrival, Meredov, who is also the deputy chairman of Turkmenistan’s cabinet of ministers, was received by Pakistan’s Ambassador to Turkmenistan and other officials, the FO said.The foreign minister of Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Tahsin Ertugruloglu, had landed in Pakistan on Saturday for the meeting.According toAPP, incumbent ECO Secretary General Asad Majeed Khan chaired a meeting on the draft agenda of the 30th ECO-COM.This gathering of senior officials from ECO member states was set to review the organisation’s activities and programmes, assess the work of its subsidiary bodies and finalise the agenda and draft outcome documents for consideration by the ministers.Monday’s ministerial meeting will be chaired by DPM Dar and attended by foreign ministers and heads of delegations from ECO member states, along with representatives of the organisation’s secretariat and subsidiary bodies.Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, will seek to advance the organisation’s objectives under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO”, the FO said in astatementon Saturday.It said Pakistan’s chairmanship would focus on strengthening regional connectivity and integration, deepening partnerships and promoting collective efforts for economic prosperity and sustainable development.The chairmanship would also provide an opportunity to strengthen the ECO’s role as a platform for regional cooperation, dialogue and economic collaboration, it added.According to the FO, Pakistan also aims to position itself as a regional connectivity hub, facilitate logistics supply chains and help shape the agenda for regional trade.The efforts would help unlock the region’s economic potential and translate the benefits of regional cooperation into tangible improvements in the lives of people in ECO member states, the statement said.Dar meets ECO, OIC, CICA headsOn the sidelines of the meeting, DPM Dar met Ambassador Majeed, FO said.Dar underscored the importance of strengthening “regional cooperation, connectivity and economic integration” within the ECO region. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to hosting the ECO Summit in 2027, the FO said.He also appreciated the ECO secretariat’s efforts in advancing the agenda of the organisation, and its support for Pakistan’s priorities during its chairmanship.“The secretary general appreciated Pakistan’s excellent arrangements, hospitality and coordination for the 30th ECO-COM and congratulated Pakistan on its upcoming chairmanship and hosting of the ECO-COM and ECO Summit in 2027, reflecting the importance Pakistan attaches to regionalism and multilateral cooperation,” the statement said.It added that both sides reaffirmed the importance of close coordination during Pakistan’s chairmanship “to ensure effective implementation of agreed initiatives and advance shared goals of regional development and prosperity”.DPM Dar also held a meeting with the OIC secretary general, welcoming him on his first visit to Islamabad since assuming office this year, the FO said.He “reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening the OIC as a unified and effective voice of the Muslim Ummah” and assured Ahmed of Pakistan’s continued support and cooperation in advancing the OIC’s objectives.“The secretary general appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts during the Iran-US conflict to promote peace and stability in the region. He also commended Pakistan’s active role in the OIC, including its contributions through COMSTECH to promoting scientific and technological cooperation among member states,” the FO said.Both sides agreed to maintain close cooperation within the OIC, while also reiterating “their steadfast support for the peoples of Palestine and Jammu and Kashmir and the realisation of their right to self-determination”, it added.The deputy premier also met with the secretary general of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA), Ambassador Sultan Hajiyev, where he reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for CICA and its efforts to promote peace, security and stability in Asia through dialogue and confidence-building measures.Hajiyev appreciated Pakistan’s constructive efforts in promoting dialogue and de-escalation. He also thanked Pakistan “for its warm hospitality and excellent arrangements” for the council meeting, the FO said.Separately, the ECO secretary general also met Deputy FM Tursunkulov to discuss Kyrgyzstan’s “contributions and ECO’s work in a range of areas including trade, energy, industry and tourism cooperation”, he said.

headline: Sales tax gets new enforcement structure to cut collection gap
summary: ISLAMABAD: After 17 years of integration, the government has decided to reverse the functional integration of sales tax and income tax collection, acknowledging that the sales tax revenue gap has widened to Rs3.4 trillion amid weak enforcement and poor revenue collection.The decision marks a major reform in tax administration, providing for the selection of officers within the Inland Revenue Service (IRS) and the separation of functional responsibilities, including tax collection and legal matters, to address persistent weaknesses that have contributed to the revenue gap, senior tax officials told Dawn on Saturday.At the chief commissioner level, the administrative structure for sales tax and income tax will remain unchanged for now. However, functional separation will begin at the commissioner level and extend to subordinate officers, with dedicated officials assigned exclusively to sales tax matters.A dedicated member for sales tax and federal excise duty will report directly to the FBR chairman. The new member, with three chiefs and their teams, will give sales tax and federal excise duty continuous attention through data analysis, operations, and follow-up on selected cases.Government will separate sales and income tax functions within IRSWithin each chief commissioner’s jurisdiction, separate sales tax zones will be established, headed by commissioners and supported by additional deputy and assistant commissioners. The restructuring will begin at Large Taxpayer Offices on Dec 1, followed by Corporate Tax Offices and Regional Tax Offices. The transition is expected to be completed within two months.The chief commissioners and Member IRS (Operations) will retain administrative and operational control, while the newly designated member will provide technical oversight and coordinate enforcement activities. Both taxes will continue to be administered within the IRS, rather than through separate services.As part of the process, the FBR has begun conducting specialised tests to identify officers with the required expertise in sales tax and income tax administration. “We have already launched an exercise to identify competent officers,” an official said, adding that the assessment would help assign officers to functions matching their professional capabilities.The need for functional separation also emerged from the widening sales tax revenue gap despite its relatively small taxpayer base. Sales tax accounts for nearly 55pc of the combined Rs6.2tr revenue gap, while approximately 90pc of its collections come from just 15,000 taxpayers, according to internal FBR estimates.Official figures showed that around 313,000 persons were registered for sales tax in early 2024, of whom only 190,000 filed tax returns, including many declaring no taxable transactions. In comparison, the number of active income tax return filers stood at approximately 6 million.It was pointed out that the integrated administrative structure had also weakened accountability, as IRS officers could meet their combined revenue targets by concentrating on income tax collections, while paying less attention to sales tax enforcement.A recent proficiency test conducted in Karachi further exposed the imbalance, with officers performing better in practical income tax matters than in sales tax administration, reflecting their greater exposure to income tax work.The FBR’s experience with production monitoring also demonstrated the benefits of targeted enforcement. In 12 manufacturing sectors where monitoring systems were introduced, the revenue gap declined by 12 percentage points of potential collections over two years, while it increased by nine percentage points in seven sectors without such systems.Under the new arrangement, specialised officers will analyse this information and pursue cases involving underreported sales, questionable input tax claims, and other compliance failures, rather than dividing their attention between income tax and sales tax responsibilities.In 2009, the then government, as part of the World Bank project, transferred the administration of sales tax and federal excise from Customs to the IRS. The major reasons for integration were that the two taxes are closely linked, because what an officer finds in a sales tax case often gives rise to an income tax demand, and that placing them under different officers would break this link.However, after 17 years of integration, official data showed substantial revenue gaps in both taxes, raising questions about the arrangement’s effectiveness. The sales tax revenue gap was estimated at Rs3.4tr, compared with Rs2tr for income tax.Officials said the original justification for integration had also weakened with the introduction of a common digital system operated by Pakistan Revenue Automation Ltd.Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

headline: Sindh cotton experiment faces winter test
summary: LAHORE: Pakistan’s cotton and textile supply chain is at a critical juncture, caught between grassroots climate adaptation in the fields of lower Sindh and widening statistical discrepancies in official crop reporting.The decision by growers in Sindh’s coastal districts of Thatta and Sujawal to begin cotton sowing in the second week of November marks an unusual departure from the country’s conventional agricultural calendar.However, whether this farmer-led experiment translates into commercial relief for the domestic textile industry depends as much on agronomic resilience through the winter as on resolving data distortions that are currently clouding market pricing.Traditionally, cotton sowing in Punjab takes place between May and June, while Sindh begins in February and March — a cycle that exposes the crop to peak summer heat stress and post-monsoon pest attacks, particularly from the pink bollworm. By utilising land cleared after the paddy harvest and intercropping directly into standing tomato fields, growers in coastal Sindh are attempting a multi-season model.Dr Tasawwar Hussain Malik, a plant breeding and genetics specialist at the Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI) in Sakrand, notes that while the initiative originated with farmers, CCRI researchers are closely monitoring the fields and conducting parallel trials to assess the viability of “off-season” planting in frost-free pockets of lower Sindh, where winter temperatures remain comparatively mild.November sowing in coastal areas could bring early lint supplies, but crop resilience and fibre quality remain uncertainIf the November-sown crop matures through winter and yields lint by February and March, domestic spinners could see fresh arrivals months ahead of the traditional August peak. Such an early injection of raw material would bridge the annual inter-season supply gap and curb reliance on costly imported lint.For ginning factories, a March start would also extend operational capacity beyond their usual three-to-four-month window, though overlapping with the late wheat harvest could strain local transport, labour and warehousing.Despite initial optimism, cotton scientists urge caution against declaring November sowing a proven model before the crop completes its full cycle.Sajid Mahmood, head of technology transfer at CCRI in Multan, points out that while daytime temperatures of 33-34 degrees Celsius and night-time lows of 21-22°C in mid-November appear favourable for germination, air temperature alone does not govern crop success.Seed germination requires warm soil at seed depth, and the decisive test will arrive between December and February. Falling night and soil temperatures during peak winter can retard root development, delay flowering, and impair boll formation.Furthermore, prolonged fog, dew, and cool, overly moist soil heighten the risk of the Seedling Disease Complex, driven by soil-borne pathogens such as Rhizoctonia and Pythium, alongside fungal leaf infections.From an industrial standpoint, sub-optimal winter warmth and reduced sunlight can compromise fibre maturity, lowering micronaire values and staple length. Should early-spring lint fail to meet export-grade spinning specifications, textile mills would inevitably discount the crop, eroding farmer profitability.Equally concerning is the potential disruption to natural pest cycles. Keeping cotton plants in the ground from November until the conventional spring sowing season could create a continuous green bridge for pink bollworm larvae to multiply and migrate into the main summer crop, he warns, stressing that multi-location comparative trials over at least two to three seasons — tracking soil temperatures, fog days, pest dynamics, and fibre quality alongside strict crop-residue management — are essential before scaling up off-season cultivation.Compounding these field uncertainties is a stark reporting gap for the 2026-27 season. While the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association recorded Punjab arrivals at 1.999 million bales by Oct 31, the Punjab Crop Reporting Service (CRS) projected provincial output at 3.7m bales, claiming arrivals reached 3.64m bales by Nov 5.This over 1.6-million-bale discrepancy distorts price discovery across the value chain. Inflated official supply estimates artificially depress local lint prices — currently hovering around Rs18,500 per maund — making growers and ginners hesitant to sell.Simultaneously, overstated projections risk delaying spinners’ forward import contracts, exposing mills to panic buying on global spot markets at steep premiums if domestic shortfalls emerge, while driving up bank risk premiums and borrowing costs for warehouse financing.Ultimately, translating coastal Sindh’s November sowing into lasting relief for Pakistan’s textile sector requires institutional alignment: targeted PARC-CCRI seed research for cold-tolerant, pest-resistant varieties paired with credible, unified crop statistics to restore market stability.Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

headline: Gas output halves in 10 years, says SSGC chief
summary: KARACHI: The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) has been forced to restrict supply to domestic consumers three meal times a day because of depleting indigenous production over the past decade, its managing director said on Saturday.According to Muhammad Amin Rajput, the schedule was necessary as the country’s gas production had fallen about 50 per cent over the last decade, while imported LNG supplies, too, were hard to come by since April due to the Iran war.“By focusing on supply during cooking hours, the company can protect domestic consumers,” the managing director said in an exclusive interview with Dawn.He said SSGC’s gas availability had fallen to around 605 million cubic feet per day due to depletion in gas fields, compared with 695mmcfd last year. “Of this, around 300mmcfd is being given to domestic consumers, while the rest is supplied to industry, power and fertiliser sectors,” Mr Rajput added.The utility has decided to supply gas during the breakfast, lunch and dinner windows to ensure that every household got the fuel when it mattered most. “The SSGC has been monitoring availability continuously since last week,” Mr Rajput said.Supply to households restricted to three meal timesHe said domestic gas supply in the city was adequate. Residents in many areas, however, complained the flame was too low for cooking purposes.“A localised issue should not be generalised across the entire network that serves roughly 50,000 kilometres of pipelines, 16,000 of them in Karachi alone. The SSGC has 3.2 million customers across Sindh and Balochistan, including two million in Karachi,” Mr Rajput observed.Use of compressors, pumpsThe SSGC MD blamed the low pressure on the illegal use of gas compressors and suction pumps. These devices can drain away the supply to an entire block or building, he cautioned. “Besides being illegal, substandard devices pose safety risks and have caused property damage, and sometimes even loss of life.”Mr Rajput urged consumers to report such use, saying that removing the devices would help restore pressure during supply hours, even though they may inflate bills by distorting meter readings.He said his company had rehabilitated about 7,000 kilometres of distribution pipelines in 2025-26, replacing ageing and corroded pipes, mostly in Karachi. “That has improved pressure at tail-end locations and reduced unaccounted-for gas.”He said the situation was further compounded by substantially reduced availability of RLNG supplies from Qatar. “Besides meeting domestic requirements, the Petroleum Division has secured limited gas supplies to meet other critical needs. These include the power and fertiliser sectors,” the SSGC chief said.These competing requirements call for prudent management and judicious allocation of available resources.Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

headline: Govt paying banks less could mean lower taxes for citizens. Here's how
summary: https://www.dawn.com/news/2044872/taxpayers-burden
content: IN challenging times, ordinary citizens and businesses may be called upon to shoulder higher tax burdens to meet the unavoidable costs of maintaining a sovereign state. But citizens should not be expected to bear the burden of costs that are largely avoidable. When debt servicing consumes 125 per cent of the FBR taxes retained by the federal government, 68.5pc of its total revenues, and nearly three times the defence budget, such an extraordinary burden demands closer scrutiny. Is our public debt being managed prudently and efficiently? In Pakistan, where a large proportion of the population comprises practising Muslims, many people prefer to keep their savings in bank accounts that pay no interest. As a result, nearly 40pc of all bank deposits are held in current accounts, on which banks pay no interest. This gives Pakistani banks access to an exceptionally cheap source of funds, which they invest in government securities at exorbitantly high returns. According to the State Bank of Pakistan, banks paid an average interest rate of just 5.53pc on their total deposits in September 2026, including current accounts that pay no interest. Yet, in October 2026, the government was borrowing through 12-month treasury bills at 12.79pc — a gross difference of 7.26 percentage points. Is our public debt being managed prudently and efficiently? A prudent borrower would certainly have sought to negotiate a much narrower margin, perhaps 1-2 percentage points. Yet our government continues to borrow at substantially higher rates, raising serious questions about the management of public debt. Ultimately, taxpayers are asked to bear the cost of such generosity. The burden falls on petrol and diesel consumers paying the Petroleum Development Levy, as well as investors paying effective income tax rates of 50-60pc. High returns on relatively low-risk government securities have encouraged banks to attract more low-cost deposits, particularly current accounts. By June 2026, these accounts held Rs15.3 trillion, nearly 40pc of total deposits, up from 37pc a year earlier. SBP confirms that the Rs3.67tn increase in deposits during the first half of 2026 came mainly from current accounts. While much of Pakistan’s productive economy has struggled, bank deposits have tripled from Rs13.35tn in December 2018 to nearly Rs41tn in September 2026. But where has this enormous pool of savings gone? Into new industries, businesses and jobs, or increasingly into high-yield government securities, earning banks substantial returns at taxpayers’ expense? According to SBP, commercial banks held Rs40.36tn in government securities in September 2026. Applying the prevailing gross interest-rate differential of 7.26 percentage points to these holdings gives an estimated annualised differential of approximately Rs2.93tn. If government borrowing rates were limited to 1-2 percentage points above banks’ average deposit cost, the estimated annualised gross savings could reach Rs2,100-2,500 billion, subject to debt maturities and repricing. Even part of these savings could ease the lives of millions of households and thousands of struggling entrepreneurs by reducing the Petroleum Development Levy, multiple taxes on energy bills, and high income tax rates on salaries and businesses. Such a policy would also reduce SBP’s annual interest earnings by approximately Rs118bn, which would be just a fraction of the overall savings. What needs to be done? The government should introduce a law that limits the interest paid to commercial banks on government securities to a reasonable 1-2 percentage points above what banks pay their depositors on average. The implementation process should ensure that monetary policy, government borrowing operations and financial stability are not disrupted. In order to bring transparency into debt management operations, the law should require the Ministry of Finance and SBP to publish quarterly reports showing how much the government borrows from banks and other investors, the interest it pays, and the cost of funds to banks. These reports should also disclose how much the government actually saves through lower borrowing costs. The potential annual savings of Rs2,100-2,500bn, once realised, should be passed on to taxpayers and businesses that have long borne the burden of excessive taxation, rather than being absorbed by increased government expenditure. The priority should be to reduce the Petroleum Development Levy and General Sales Tax on electricity bills, thereby lowering fuel and transport costs, easing the cost of living and production, and reducing inflationary pressures. The government should also double the annual income-tax exemption threshold from Rs600,000 to Rs1.2 million, providing much-needed relief to salaried individuals and low-income taxpayers. The government should also restore the Final Tax Regime for exporters, making tax deducted from export proceeds their final income tax liability, even if the rate remains 2pc. This would simplify taxation, eliminate uncertainty and improve the competitiveness of Pakistani exporters by bringing their tax treatment closer to that of competitors in peer economies. Equally important is the complete abolition of the super tax, which reportedly generates around Rs400-500bn annually, but has become a major deterrent to new investment. The highest effective income tax rate on corporate, business and other incomes should be capped at 35pc, making Pakistan more attractive to investors while leaving greater disposable income available for savings, consumption and investment. Many such measures could be financed through the proposed annual debt-servicing savings of Rs2,100-2,500bn, provided the government pursues the necessary reforms with determination and ensures that the resulting fiscal space is used to reduce the tax burden rather than expand public expenditure. These measures would provide a much-needed stimulus to economic growth, encourage investment and job creation, and help alleviate poverty, which has become one of the country’s most pressing challenges. Reviving economic growth requires reducing the excessive tax burden on ordinary citizens and businesses — a burden that stifles investment, discourages enterprise and holds back economic activity. The writer is former federal finance secretary and currently chairman, Policy Research and Advisory Council. Published in Dawn, November 16th, 2026

headline: Another bullish week as stocks flirt with 180,000-milestone
summary: KARACHI: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended its recovery rally during the outgoing week as falling international oil prices eased inflation concerns and encouraged value-hunting across the board.The index crossed the 180,000-point barrier during the second-last trading session but failed to sustain gains as investors resorted to profit-taking. Cautious sentiment amid domestic political uncertainty also capped the rally.According to Arif Habib Ltd (AHL), the KSE-100 index gained 3,987 points, or 2.29 per cent, week-on-week to close at 177,873.88 points on Friday. It traded between an intra-week high of 180,769 and a low of 176,292 points.Topline Securities attributed the positive performance primarily to declining crude oil prices and improved investor sentiment amid hopes of a de-escalation in Middle East tensions following the US midterm election results.Falling oil prices, higher remittances and institutional buying support marketInternational oil prices retreated sharply during the week, with Brent crude easing to around $96.10 per barrel by Friday. The decline from elevated levels helped ease concerns about imported inflation and the domestic economic outlook.Among major economic developments, workers’ remittances rose 14pc year-on-year to $3.9 billion in October, compared to $3.4bn in the corresponding month last year. Inflows also increased 8pc month-on-month, taking cumulative remittances during the first four months of FY27 to $14.8bn, up 14pc from a year earlier.Pakistan posted a fiscal surplus of Rs1,274bn, equivalent to 0.9pc of gross domestic product, during the first quarter of FY27, down 40pc from Rs2,119bn, or 1.7pc of GDP, in the same period last year. The primary surplus stood at Rs3 trillion. Federal Board of Revenue collection amounted to Rs3,086bn, up 7pc year-on-year, while markup payments increased 23pc to Rs1,700bn.In the latest treasury bill auction, the government raised Rs587bn, exceeding its Rs400bn target, while cut-off yields declined by 22 to 48 basis points across tenors. Meanwhile, central government debt fell 1pc during the first quarter of the current fiscal year to Rs82.7tr as of Sept 30.The State Bank of Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves increased by $11.3 million to $21.6bn as of Nov 6, while banks’ reserves declined by $37.1m to $5.3bn. Total liquid foreign exchange reserves stood at $26.8bn, providing import cover of approximately three months.On the energy front, petroleum prices declined by around Rs21 per litre to Rs332 and high-speed diesel by Rs22 to Rs360 per litre.Weekly oil production edged up 0.5pc to 65,200 barrels per day, while gas output increased 3.3pc to 3,106 million cubic feet per day, supported by higher production from Uch, Kandhkot, Naimat West and Sutiari Deep fields.Automobile sales also recorded strong growth. Passenger car sales rose sharply in October, with industry data indicating increased demand, particularly for lower-displacement vehicles. The Pakistan Automotive Manufacturers Association reported sales of 21,635 units, up 60pc year-on-year. The rupee appreciated marginally by 0.02pc against the dollar, closing at Rs276.60 compared to Rs276.66 in the preceding week.Sector-wise, exploration and production companies led the gains, contributing 1,058 points to the benchmark index, followed by banks with 1,036 points, cement (545 points), fertiliser (317 points) and investment banks (187 points).Among individual stocks, Mari Petroleum contributed the most, adding 582 points, followed by United Bank (264 points), Lucky Cement (250 points), Pakistan Petroleum (244 points) and Habib Bank (202 points). National Bank led the negative contributors, shedding 48 points, followed by Attock Refinery, Adamjee Insurance, Pakistan Telecommunication and Cnergyico.AHL expects the market to maintain a cautiously optimistic trajectory, with further gains possible if international oil prices remain stable.Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

headline: Fiscal surplus shrinks 40pc as revenues decline
summary: • Primary surplus drops to 2.1pc of GDP from 2.8pc last year• Revenue falls despite higher tax collections; interest payments jump 23pc• Provincial cash surpluses shrink 23pc; Balochistan posts deficitISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s fiscal buffers weakened in the first quarter of the current fiscal year despite expenditure controls and subsidy cuts, as revenue-to-GDP ratios declined and provincial cash surpluses shrank.The overall fiscal surplus fell to 0.9 per cent of GDP in July-September this year from 1.7pc a year ago, according to fiscal operations data released by the Ministry of Finance.In absolute terms, the surplus declined by 40pc to Rs1.273 trillion in the first three months of the current fiscal year compared to Rs2.12tr a year earlier.The primary surplus — the difference between total revenue and expenditure excluding interest payments — also narrowed to 2.1pc of GDP from 2.8pc in the corresponding period last year. It stood at Rs2.97tr, down 15pc from Rs3.5tr in the first quarter of the previous fiscal year.Total revenue declined to 4.2pc of GDP from 4.9pc a year earlier. In a rare happening, revenue also fell in absolute terms to Rs6.004tr from Rs6.2tr, despite inflationary pressures and nominal economic growth that normally contribute to higher collections.The deterioration was reflected in both tax and non-tax revenue ratios, although the larger decline came from non-tax revenue, which fell to 1.8pc of GDP (Rs2.6tr) by the end of September 2026 compared to 2.4pc (Rs3.046tr) a year earlier.This was mainly due to lower State Bank profits, which dropped to Rs1.933tr from Rs2.43tr. However, petroleum receipts increased slightly to Rs382bn from Rs372bn.Tax revenue slipped to 2.4pc of GDP from 2.5pc a year earlier, although collections increased in absolute terms to Rs3.387tr from Rs3.153tr.On the expenditure side, total spending increased both as a percentage of GDP and in absolute terms.The expenditure-to-GDP ratio rose to 3.3pc from 3.2pc, while total expenditure increased by 16pc to Rs4.73tr from Rs4.08tr last year.Current expenditure declined as a share of GDP to 3pc from 3.2pc, although it increased in absolute terms to Rs4.293tr from Rs4.047tr.A major contributor to higher spending was the increase in interest payments, which rose by more than 23pc to Rs1.7tr from Rs1.378tr. As a share of GDP, these payments increased to 1.2pc from 1.1pc.Defence expenditure declined as a share of GDP to 0.3pc from 0.4pc, although it rose in absolute terms to Rs496bn from Rs447bn.Development expenditure remained unchanged at 0.3pc of GDP but increased to Rs468bn from Rs440bn.The data showed that subsidies were curtailed to Rs84.6bn (0.2pc of GDP) compared to Rs120bn (0.3pc) in the same period last year.Pension expenditure and the cost of running the civil government increased by 10pc and 6pc to Rs495bn and Rs263bn, respectively.Meanwhile, cash surpluses generated by the four provincial governments declined by 23pc to Rs600bn from Rs781bn last year.Punjab’s surplus fell to Rs333bn from Rs442bn, while Sindh’s surplus declined to Rs181bn from Rs209bn.However, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa increased its surplus by 33pc to Rs102bn from Rs77bn. Balochistan recorded a Rs16bn deficit in the first quarter against a surplus of Rs53bn in the corresponding period last year.The Ministry of Finance also reported a statistical discrepancy of Rs60bn in provincial accounts and attributed it to uncleared or delayed payments, late presentation of cheques relating to assignment accounts and movements in commercial bank deposits.A federal statistical discrepancy of Rs98bn was attributed to reporting time lags, book adjustments involving the State Bank of Pakistan, Federal Board of Reve­nue and Economic Affairs Division and a decline in commercial bank deposits.Published in Dawn, November 14th, 2026

headline: Musk says Nvidia will lose 'critical' deals without Jensen Huang
summary: Elon Musk said on Saturday that chipmaker Nvidia would lose “critical” deals without its now-ousted chief executive officer (CEO) Jensen Huang.Huangstepped downon Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including oneinvolvinga suspectedChinesespy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.In a post on X, Musk said that while Huang drove the supply chain “brilliantly” at Nvidia, many such deals were “a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract”.“Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost.”The SpaceX boss went on to praise the former Nvidia CEO: “If Jensen gave me his word about compute delivery or I asked for components to be accelerated, he always came through.“Sure, we’d put together a purchase order at some point later, but I never for a second thought it wouldn’t happen.”The billionaire has separately said on X that a petition was underway to reinstate Huang and that he would sign it. It was not immediately clear whether Musk was referring to the internal effort reported byWired.Nvidia declined to comment on theWiredreport as well as Musk’s post.Reuterscould not independently verify the reports.Pressure had mounted on Huang afterreportssaid the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair withAlice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities had been investigating.Nvidia then said its board was probing whether its then-CEO “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”.On Thursday,CNNreportedthat the US intelligence community was still working to understand the relationship between Alice Huang and the Chinese government, with multiple sources tellingCNNthat the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove that she was acting as a spy for Beijing.The report said there was “disagreement among US officials about the strength of the evidence that Alice Huang was recruited by the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS)” to spy on Jensen Huang.Insiders and tech titans in the runningHuang’s exit plunges the $4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia’s swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry’s biggest labs.Nvidia’s board hasapproachedBritish chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang, theFinancial Timesreported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.Haas’s name has been making the rounds among analysts since Huang’s exit. He spent seven formative years at Nvidia, rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business, before joining Arm in 2013.Nvidia’s finance chiefColette Kressis currently interim CEO.Nvidia’s board said it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the CEO role and had not formally engaged any potential candidates.Some analysts expect the next CEO to break from Huang’s three-decade reign as the hands-on “chief conductor” who personally steered engineering roadmaps, geopolitical negotiations over exports to China and massive investments across the AI ecosystem.A potential shift toward a more institutional leadership structure would come as Nvidia faces heightened regulatory scrutiny and a growing consensus among US lawmakers to further restrict the company’s chip exports to China.Analysts view Kress as a steady financial authority, while veteran engineer Ian Buck is seen as a top candidate after leading development of CUDA, the software platform that powers Nvidia’s AI chips.Apart from Haas, external names discussed by analysts include AMD chief Lisa Su, who has navigated the key China market, and Micron chief Sanjay Mehrotra, whose memory chips power Nvidia servers.Other candidates cited by industry watchers include Marvell head Matt Murphy and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, who oversaw the iPhone maker’s in-house silicon development.Former Apple chief Tim Cook was floated by US President Donald Trump, as Nvidia’s board evaluates whether to prioritise financial continuity, deep technical expertise, or experience running a global tech heavyweight.

headline: Tarar says referendum 'legal and constitutional' method of gauging public opinion on new provinces
summary: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Tuesday that a referendum was a legal and constitutional method of gauging public opinion on new provinces, adding that no political party should have reservations regarding it.He made the comments in televised remarks following ahard-hitting speechby PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. The minister said that there was an ongoing debate in the country regarding “good governance”.“The public wants a good government that is accountable … You and all of us have been part of this system for decades. Today, we cannot separate ourselves from the weaknesses of the system,” he said.He said that to “enjoy the perks” being in power and also do opposition amounted to having a “double standard”. He said that the reason behind the PPP chairman’s remarks was the ongoing debate regarding provinces.“And this debate is raging among the masses. Will you silence the people? Will you stop them from talking about improving governance? headline: 'Under the bus': Feuds grip Trump's White House after midterms
summary: From feuding officials stuck together on Air Force One to uncomfortable press conferences, rifts in President Donald Trump’s White House have spilt into the open after theUS midterm elections.Disagreements over China, AI and Iran have flared up, while personal rivalries in the West Wing that were bottled up for the first half of Trump’s second term have started to boil over.Most public of all is the feud between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, over the scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy that forcedNvidia’s Jensen Huang to resign.Bessent delivered an astonishing slap-down in an interview onCNBCon Friday when he openly rebuked Lutnick’s department for failing to blacklist Megaspeed, a company formerly linked to Huang’s lover that was accused of shifting vital Nvidia chips to China.“Bessent just threw Lutnick under the bus, ran over him, backed up, and ran over him again,”Washington Postanalyst Josh Rogin wrote on X.The squabbling pair were then forced to spend nearly 20 awkward hours together in the presidential jet as Trump travelled to Asia.On the ground in Manilaon Tuesday, Lutnick and Bessent studiously ignored each other despite being seated side by side while Trump signed a trade deal with Thailand.‘Two different views’Trump played down the row and denied that he planned to fire Lutnick. Yet at the same time he admitted a rift at the heart of his administration’s China policy just days before asummitwith Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.“They’re fine. They have two different views,” Trump told anAFPreporter as he left the White House on Monday when asked about Bessent and Lutnick’s relationship.“One wants to be friendly with China, and one wants to have a blow-up with China.”The White House denied any disunity.“President Trump has assembled the most talented and impressive cabinet in history and they are doing an excellent job carrying out the President’s agenda. Efforts by the legacy media to sow internal division is a distraction that will not work,” White House spokesman Davis Ingle said in a statement toAFP.“All agencies across this administration have and will continue to be in lockstep with President Trump’s mission to deliver results for the American people.”The midterms have already claimed their first scalp in the West Wing, after Trumpnamedimmigration hardliner Stephen Miller to replace so-called “ice maiden” Susie Wiles as his chief of staff.And there has been jockeying for position as speculation swirls about who could be next.‘Besties’An example came on Friday as Trump’s administration struggled to get to grips with a mass air travel shutdown.The White House put Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security chief Markwayne Mullin at the podium in front of reporters — but their double act did not entirely go to plan.Duffy appeared to shake his head and gently nudge his colleague’s elbow when Mullin said that new “patches” were overwhelming old equipment — contradicting the transport chief’s assertion that it was only the ageing gear that was to blame.TheIran warhas also been a source of tension.Vice President JD Vance said the day after the midterms that “the reason we lost is the war,” apparently seeking to distance himself from the conflict ahead of a possible presidential run in 2028.Trump denied Vance’s comments had affected their relationship. Yet he told reporters on Nov 8 that “a lot of people didn’t like his comments” — before adding: “But not me.” Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth, who has fought off an impeachment bid for now over the Iran war, also subtly sought to distance himself from Vance’s comments.“I respect the vice president greatly, and I’m certainly not going to engage in any finger-pointing,” Hegseth said last week, before adding that the Iran war was “not necessarily popular, but it may have been necessary.”Still, it’s not all knives out at the White House.Miller, the new chief of staff, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have struck up an “unlikely alliance” after being foes during Trump’s first term, the Wall Street Journal reported.Miller’s wife, Katie, told the paper that the two men were now “besties”.

headline: PTA finalises licensing framework for 'sky-high' internet, telecommunication services
summary: The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) said on Tuesday that it had finalised a licensing framework for satellite-based in-flight telecommunication services, “paving way for internet connectivity and other digital services aboard aircraft”.“Under the framework, licensed in-flight telecommunication services providers would be able to use satellites to offer connectivity to Pakistani-registered aircraft, subject to registration with the Pakistan Space Activities Regulatory Board and compliance with PTA’s licensing requirements,” the authority said in a press release on Tuesday.It added that transit aircraft passing through Pakistani airspace would require a no-objection certificate from the authority, subject to applicable compliance requirements.It said that the introduction of in-flight telecommunication services would “enhance passenger experience through seamless in-flight internet connectivity, enabling access to digital services, entertainment, personal communication and work-related activities”.It added that the initiative would further strengthen the authority’s efforts to expand digital connectivity in Pakistan by “extending telecommunication services beyond terrestrial networks and enabling seamless connectivity during air travel”.

headline: Local govt polls in Punjab to be held in two phases
summary: ISLAMABAD: Local government polls in Punjab, which are scheduled for February 2027, will be held in two phases, it emerged on Tuesday.In a letter to the Punjab chief secretary, the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) said it had accepted the proposal conveyed by the province’s Local Government and Community Development Department secretary, in his letter dated Nov 16.According to the letter seen byDawn, the commission also directed its office to proceed with the conduct of local government elections and ensure timely completion of all prerequisite activities.Under the agreed plan, elections will be held in 18 districts in each phase.The first phase will cover Chakwal and Talagang, Pakpattan, Sialkot, Okara, Rajanpur, Narowal, Chiniot, Khanewal, Nankana Sahib, Kasur, Rawalpindi and Murree, Dera Ghazi Khan and Taunsa, Lahore, Bahawalpur, Lodhran, Sargodha, Hafizabad and Bhakkar.The second phase will cover Sahiwal, Gujranwala and Wazirabad, Bahawalnagar, Attock, Khushab, Mandi Bahauddin, Vehari, Jhelum, Sheikhupura, Muzaffargarh and Kot Addu, Toba Tek Singh, Faisalabad, Multan, Mianwali, Layyah, Jhang, Gujrat and Rahim Yar Khan.The ECP also forwarded copies of the letter to the provincial election commissioner and the secretary of the Punjab Local Government and Community Development Department.The last local government elections in Punjab were held in 2015 under thePunjab Local Government Act, 2013. Polling took place in phases between October and December 2015, and elected councils assumed office in 2017 after indirect elections for mayors and chairpersons. Since then, local body polls in Punjab have experienced repeated delays.The PTI government had dissolved the elected local bodies in April 2019 before they completed their tenure. The move was later struck down by the Supreme Court, which restored them. They eventually completed their term on Dec 31, 2021.Successive provincial governments repeatedly amended or replaced the Punjab Local Government Act. Each legislative change required the ECP to restart preparations, including delimitation and election planning.Changing laws and administrative delaysby successive governments contributed significantly to the postponement of the local body elections.Under Article 140A of the Constitution and the Elections Act, local government elections should be held within 120 days of the expiry of local bodies’ terms. Since the councils’ term ended in Dec 2021, elections were due by April 2022, but they have been repeatedly postponed.The ECP had initiallyproposedholding elections in Punjab on Dec 14. However, the provincial government had instead proposed elections in phases in April 2027, citing smog, dense fog and adverse winter weather conditions expected during December and January.The ECP hadrejectedthe proposal and, earlier this month,decidedto hold the first phase of polls in Punjab on Feb 7, 2027. The decision came following a hearing conducted by a four-member bench headed by Chief Election Commission Sikandar Sultan Raja.During the hearing, an ECP member pointed out that the provincial government had previously proposed holding elections in April.However, the provincial chief secretary responded that the government had reconsidered its position and had no objection to elections in January or February, although April would be more suitable because of longer daylight hours and school holidays.

headline: Vehicles without fitness, emission tests to be barred from Islamabad to curb smog
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government on Tuesday decided to barvehicleswithout fitness and emission testing from entering Islamabad, as part of measures to curb smog and air pollution in the capital.The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry to review steps for smog prevention and reduction of air pollution.The meeting reviewed the current smog situation in Islamabad, the Air Quality Index (AQI) and ongoing measures to control air pollution.Chaudhry directed all relevant departments to ensure coordinated and effective measures to control air pollution and prevent smog. He said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi was himself monitoring the entire process of anti-smog measures in Islamabad and their implementation.He contended that Islamabad’s AQI in October and November this year had remained better than the same period last year.According to data published by the Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency (Pak-EPA), the averageAQI indexfor Islamabad was 148 thisOctober, compared to an average of 169 inOctober 2025.During the meeting, it was decided that heavy fines would be imposed on those involved in open burning and other smog-causing activities.Chaudhry warned of first information reports, arrests and heavy fines against violators of environmental laws. Strict action would also be taken against smoke-emitting brick kilns and industrial units, he added.The minister stressed that public cooperation was crucial for smog control and improvement in air quality, and citizens would have to play a responsible role.The additional deputy commissioner (ADC) (General), ADC (Revenue), the senior superintendent of police (Operations) and the chief traffic officer attended the meeting, alongside the Pak-EPA and excise directors and other relevant officials.In the past few years, air pollution has become one of the most pressing public health and environmental crises facing Pakistan. Variouscitiesdeal with smog, attributed mainly to industrial emissions,vehicular pollution,stubble burningandair movement.Last month, a two-day Pakistan National Clean Air Conferenceconcludedwith the adoption of the Islamabad Clean Air Compact, calling for coordinated federal and provincial action, stricter enforcement, regular emissions inventories and annual reviews to tackle air pollution.The National Assembly Standing Committee on Climate Change and Environmental Coordination hasrecommendedthe introduction of a regular vehicle emission testing mechanism in Islamabad and called for updating the Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997, to bring it in line with current environmental challenges and international commitments.Last year, Pak-EPAlaunchedlarge-scale inspections ofvehiclesand industrial units, while demolishing non-compliant brick kilns as part of a multi-tier plan to curb escalating air pollution.

headline: 8 Pakistan Bar Council members call on judiciary to take note of Imran's plea for medical treatment
summary: ISLAMABAD: Eight members of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) on Tuesday called upon the judiciary to ensure implementation of the Supreme Court’s (SC) order directing incarcerated ex-premier Imran Khan’s transfer to Shifa International Hospital for medical treatment.OnAug 18, a three-member SC bench had directed the government to shift Imran to SIH within the next two days as it heard several petitions concerning his health. However, the government took the PTI founder to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences for acheck-upand then transported him back to prison.On Monday, in anopen letterto the chief justices of the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), the SC and the Islamabad High Court (IHC), Imran appealed for medical treatment for himself and Bushra Bibi. He also said that he would only be able to prove his innocence in the various cases against him “if I stay alive”.In a statement issued on Tuesday, eight members of the PBC said: “We call upon the judiciary to take up the former prime minister’s plea immediately and to save his and his wife’s lives by ensuring that court orders are implemented, that proper medical treatment is provided and that due process and a fair trial are guaranteed as mandated by the Constitution.”The statement was signed by Abid Shahid Zuberi, Muhammad Maqsood Buttar, Shafqat Mehmood Chauhan, Abdul Sattar Khan, Munir Ahmed Kakar, Salman Akram Raja, Salahuddin Ahmed and Qazi Muhammad Arshad.The PBC members urged the government and its agencies to implement court orders and ensure that both Imran and his wife received proper medical treatment in accordance with the law and the Constitution. The statement warned that the government and its agencies would be solely responsible for “imperilling” the lives and liberty of the couple.“We the undersigned reserve our right to initiate legal proceedings to protect the life, liberty, and constitutional and legal rights of Imran and Bushra Bibi,” the statement said.The statement also condemned “in the strongest terms” the alleged unlawful and unconstitutional treatment meted out to Imran and his wife, adding that the situation was endangering their lives, liberty and dignity.“[Imran’s] letter reveals that the former prime minister and his wife have been denied their constitutional and human rights through trumped-up and false cases and that they are incarcerated in violation of the law, the jail manual and the prison rules,” the statement asserted.The statement further added that Imran and Bushra Bibi were convicted in false cases and their appeals against these convictions had not been heard.“Even their bail applications have not been fixed for hearing,” it said.The statement further highlighted that Imran had been kept in solitary confinement and denied due medical treatment and access to his legal team and family members, jeopardising his and his wife’s health.The statement also alleged that his sisters had been detained arbitrarily and unlawfully, while the SC’s Aug 18 order had been openly flouted by the government and its agencies in violation of the law and the Constitution.“Every person in Pakistan is guaranteed the right to life and liberty under Article 9, and the right to due process and a fair trial under Article 10-A of the Constitution,” the statement said.“These rights have been denied to Imran, his wife, his family and his party members,” it said.“As patriotic Pakistanis who believe in the rule of law, we are ashamed to read Imran’s plea for implementation of the SC’s orders and for the proper medical treatment that has been denied to him and his wife,” the statement said.Moreover, the Democratic Alliance, a confederation of lawyers led by former PBC vice chairman Abid Saqi, expressed grave alarm over what it described as the deteriorating health and unlawful detention conditions of Imran and his family members.In a statement, the alliance asked the judiciary to take immediate notice of the matter and enforce its orders concerning medical treatment and access to family members.It also called on the government to end Imran’s solitary confinement, provide him with comprehensive medical treatment and release family members held without cause.The alliance’s statement further urged the international community and human rights organisations to take urgent cognisance of the “grave” situation.“The life of a former prime minister and his family hang in the balance. Justice delayed is justice denied. The Democratic Alliance demands that the rule of law and human dignity prevail before it is too late,” the statement said.Separately, the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan also expressed “deep concern” at what it called the state’s treatment of political prisoners, urging authorities to uphold their fundamental rights, irrespective of political affiliation.Referring to the allegations Imran made in his letter, the HRCP said they required urgent and independent examination.“HRCP stresses that violations of political prisoners’ fundamental freedoms are not a matter of personalities or political affiliations; they constitute an assault on the rule of law,” the commission said.“Every prisoner is entitled to humane treatment, adequate healthcare, access to family and lawyers, and a fair trial. All relevant court orders must be implemented and allegations of mistreatment independently investigated,” it added.

headline: UK sanctions Israeli firms helping build West Bank settlements
summary: Britain on Tuesday announced a slew of sanctions against eight Israeli companies helping to plan and build West Bank settlements, in a bid to halt new construction.“Do not bid, do not build, in the occupiedWest Bankwhich were put out to tender in August.And the UN secretary general has said the E1 project posed an “existential threat” to a contiguous Palestinian state.The UK’s Foreign Office said Tuesday’s “sanctions target construction and property development firms involved in settlement expansion”.“The UK has taken firm action against eight construction and property development firms which will disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support further construction in the West Bank,” it added in a statement.The move comes amid heavy criticism of Israel for blocking desperately neededsuppliesof tents and timber into the devastated Gaza Strip which has been hit by heavy flooding.Heavy rain earlier this monthswept awaytens of thousands of tents in the ravaged Palestinian territory, where virtually the entire population has been displaced at least once, according to Hamas-led authorities in Gaza.The Foreign Office, citing the UN, said “over 150,000 tents and 300,000 tarpaulins that humanitarian partners and donors purchased are outside Gaza ready to go in but are being held by the Israeli authorities”.It said the floods had led to “nearly 4,000 households left without shelter and 1.4 million people living in tents or makeshift shelters”.And it accused Israeli authorities of blocking “timber from entering, leaving no emergency shelter kits available in Gaza”.The UK’s Foreign Office also sanctioned Israeli activist group Tzav 9 on Tuesday for blocking aid deliveries into Gaza.“We will not stand by while those blocking desperately needed aid deepen the intolerable suffering of civilians in Gaza,” Miliband said.The sanctions result in asset freezes for the companies and group as well as director disqualifications.One of the blacklisted Israeli companies, real estate developer Harey Zahav, sparked controversy in 2023 when it posted a slogan on social media voicing hopes of returning settlers to Gaza.It has gained a reputation for constructing wildcat settler outposts in the occupied West Bank without Israeli government authorisation.

headline: What to expect from US-China AI safety talks?
summary: After agreeing in September to set up an AI crisis hotline, US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping will attempt this week to bring the idea closer to fruition.Threatening to steal their thunder isJensen Huang’s resignationas boss of US chip titan Nvidia after revelations of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.But with artificial intelligence developing at a rapid pace, many see cooperation on how to tackle its risks and benefits as increasingly urgent.Here’s what to expect ahead of AI safety talks between Trump and Xi at theAsia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meetingon Nov 18-19.What’s at stake?Despite the countries’ fierce tech rivalry, AI safety risks of shared concern range from infrastructure hacking to people using the technology to help build bioweapons.Another problem is out-of-control AI agents, tools that complete real-life tasks online, which came to the forefront after US lab OpenAI acknowledged its autonomous bots had hacked into websites, including an Australian government data portal.Military use and mass surveillance are also potential flashpoints for the world’s two leading AI powers.Researcher Christopher LaRochewrotein theBulletin of the Atomic Scientistson Sunday that an AI hotline could be “a step in the right direction” to help the sides communicate in cases like the OpenAI hacks.“If a similar incident entangled the United States and China — such as, for example, AI agents accessing sensitive American or Chinese infrastructure — it is unclear how Beijing or Washington would assure the other a deliberate attack was not underway,” he wrote.What did Trump and Xi agree in September?At theirlast summit in Washington, the leaders agreed to “establish a bilateral communication channel for AI incidents”, according to the Chinese foreign ministry.It said they also agreed “on the establishment of the China-US AI Dialogue to exchange views on risks and benefits related to AI”, with the next exchange to take place in November.A White House statement described the outcomes in similar terms, although it used Trump’s preferred alternative to “AI” — “SI”, which stands for “super intelligence” — and said the leaders had agreed to use that wording instead.But the effectiveness of a hotline will depend on the details.“The real questions are whether the text defines an ‘incident’ (a stolen model? an AI-enabled intrusion? a market crash?) and who sits at each end,” Stephen Wu, founder of the Carthage Capital investment fund, said in written comments toAFP.What is expected this time?US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said last week that “we… expect to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release, and for keeping human judgment firmly in command”.As AI advances, “so will the need to engage in new areas of risk management — and to demonstrate how two nations can reconcile the demands of competition with the responsibilities of leadership”.Brookings Institution fellow Kyle Chan said Trump’s confidence that the US is ahead of China in AI “gives him more leeway to feel like he can give a green light for these AI discussions”.But “a grand bargain, or some kind of arms control treaty for AI is very, very unlikely for the foreseeable future”, Chan added.Will the Nvidia scandal have an impact?Huang’s shock departure from Nvidia and scrutiny over alleged smuggling of top-end AI chips to China, where the US restricts their export for national security reasons, could be the elephant in the room.Heightening the drama, Washington announced tougher export control measures on advanced chips Monday, after the Nvidia scandal exposed a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies to develop AI.But it is unlikely to “dominate the agenda” or affect Trump and Xi’s personal relationship, predicted Dylan Loh of Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.Nicholas Cook, a lawyer focused on the AI industry and based in Hong Kong, agreed.“These developments don’t necessarily prevent constructive engagement… in Shenzhen, where shared prosperity and technology are already on the agenda,” he toldAFP.“If anything, they reinforce the need for continued dialogue to keep the two sides aligned.”

headline: Pakistan, Sri Lanka docked WTC points for slow over-rates in first Test
summary: Pakistan and Sri Lanka have been penalised for maintaining slow over-rates in thedrawn first Testof their two-match ICC World Test Championship (WTC) series, with Pakistan losing five points and Sri Lanka suffering a 15-point deduction.Match referee Dean Cosker of the ICC International Panel imposed the sanctions after Pakistan were found five overs short of the required rate and Sri Lanka 15 overs behind, after time allowances were taken into account.Under the ICC Code of Conduct, players are fined five per cent of their match fees for every over their side falls short, subject to a maximum penalty of 50 per cent. Consequently, Pakistan were fined 25 per cent of their match fees, while Sri Lanka received the maximum 50 per cent fine.Captains Babar Azam and Kusal Mendis pleaded guilty to the offences and accepted the sanctions, avoiding formal hearings. The charges were brought by on-field umpires Adrian Holdstock and Rod Tucker, third umpire Allahuddien Paleker and fourth umpire Faisal Afridi.The penalties have further dented both teams’ positions in the 2025-27 WTC cycle. Pakistan, who had moved to nine points with a points percentage of 7.50 following the Rawalpindi draw, have slipped to four points and approximately 3.33 per cent after the deduction.Sri Lanka, meanwhile, have dropped from 28 points and a percentage of 33.33 to approximately 15.48 per cent, falling to eighth place in the nine-team standings.The latest penalty adds to Pakistan’s growing problems with over-rate violations in the current WTC cycle. The team had already incurred a 19-point deduction for previous offences, including an11-point penaltyfollowing the third Test against England at Edgbaston in September.Repeated sanctions have significantly undermined Pakistan’s campaign, leaving them with little realistic prospect of qualifying for the WTC final. Their poor results, combined with successive over-rate penalties, have further complicated their position in the competition.The second Test between Pakistan and Sri Lanka began in Rawalpindi on Tuesday, giving both sides another opportunity to improve their standings. However, the points deducted following the opening match will remain a setback for the remainder of the championship cycle.

headline: Autopsy reveals multiple injuries on teenage domestic worker found dead at FIA official’s residence in Islamabad
summary: ISLAMABAD: The autopsy report of a 13-year-old domestic worker, who wasfound deadat the official residence of a senior Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) official on Sunday night, suggests that she had been subjected to repeated physical assaults.According to the first information report (FIR), the girl, identified as Fatima Asghar, allegedly died due to physical torture and violence. The suspects are the FIA official’s dual-national wife and a Qari who worked as a servant at his Islamabad residence.The autopsy report stated that the deceased had died from repeated physical assaults that caused grievous injuries and severe inflammation, leading to thromboembolism (blockage of a blood vessel by a blood clot) and cardiopulmonary arrest (cessation of heart and breathing functions).“All injuries were inflicted before death and were sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course of life,” it addedThe autopsy report documented 20 injuries on the girl’s body, all of which were suspected to have been caused by physical assault. These included swelling on the left side of the head near the temple, a blood clot on the right side of the head, a bald patch on the right side of the scalp, two old, healed scars on the right cheek, swelling and skin loss on the left cheek, a bruise on the left shoulder and a wound on the left arm.Other injuries included swelling and bruising on the left wrist, the back of the left hand and the second and third fingers; a scar between the thumb and index finger of the right hand; a scar on the outer side of the right arm; and swelling and bruising on the right hand, including the second and third fingers.The report also noted multiple old, linear dark marks on the right side of the chest and lower abdomen, as well as an old, unhealed burn mark on the left side of the back near the shoulder blade.Old burn scars on the back, a thickened scar on the right upper thigh, darkened and swollen skin around both knees and the left thigh, swelling in the knee joint and a non-healing wound on the outer side of the left knee were also found.The examination also revealed extensive swelling across the head, extending from the left temple to the back of the head, along with internal bleeding attributed to physical assault. A separate blood clot was also found on the right side of the head.The report said samples of the heart, lungs, liver, blood and stomach contents, along with other specimens, whole-body X-rays and a brain CT scan, had been handed over to the police for examination and analysis.Meanwhile, First Lady Bibi Asifa Bhutto Zardari expressed sorrow over Fatima’s death, saying that no child should be subjected to violence, abuse or exploitation.In a statement, she pointed out that Islamabad’s child employment law, enacted four years ago, prohibited the employment of children of Fatima’s age as domestic workers, even with parental consent. She stressed that the law must be enforced in letter and spirit to prevent the exploitation of children.Asifa called for a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation into the circumstances surrounding Fatima’s death and urged that those found responsible be brought to justice in accordance with the law.She also emphasised the need for collective efforts to protect vulnerable children, particularly those working in domestic settings, from abuse and exploitation.The suspects were arrested on Sunday after an FIR was registered against them under Section 302 (intentional murder) of the Pakistan Penal Code at Shams Colony police station.In the FIR, Fatima’s father, a resident of Rahim Yar Khan, said his daughter was a seminary student and was residing with close relatives at Police Lines Headquarters in Islamabad’s H-11 sector. He said he was informed in the morning that she had suddenly fallen ill and was taken to a hospital, where she died.An Islamabad police officer said Fatima had been working as a domestic help at the official’s residence for a couple of years, dating back to when he was serving in the capital police.

headline: Pakistan discusses avenues for enhancing bilateral defence cooperation with UK, Turkiye
summary: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir discussed avenues for enhancing defence cooperation with both the United Kingdom and Turkiye, in separate meetings with the British army chief and the Turkish air chief in Rawalpindi, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR)saidon Tuesday.According to the military’s media wing, a high-level delegation from the UK, led by Chief of General Staff General Sir Charles Roland Vincent Walker, called on the CDF at General Headquarters (GHQ).The visiting official was presented with a Guard of Honour by a smartly turned-out Pakistan Army contingent upon arrival.“Matters of mutual interest, the prevailing regional security environment and avenues for enhancing bilateral defence and security cooperation” were discussed in the meeting, the ISPR said. The CDF underscored Pakistan’s commitment to further expanding defence ties with the UK.“Both sides expressed satisfaction over the longstanding, cordial relations between Pakistan and the United Kingdom and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening bilateral military-to-military cooperation,” it added.The visiting dignitary, in turn, appreciated the “professionalism and operational preparedness” of Pakistan’s armed forces, acknowledging their contributions towards peace and stability in the region.According to the statement, the visit reflected the shared resolve of Pakistan and the UK to deepen defence cooperation and strengthen bilateral military ties.Separately, Commander of the Turkish Air Force General Rafet Dalkıran also called on the CDF at GHQ, where matters of mutual interest, regional security dynamics and avenues to enhance bilateral defence cooperation were discussed, the military said.CDF Munir highlighted the “deep-rooted historical, cultural and strategic ties between the two countries “and appreciated the strong defence partnership between their armed forces.The visiting dignitary reciprocated the strengthening of bilateral defence ties, appreciated the professionalism of the Pakistan Armed Forces and acknowledged the country’s contributions to regional peace and stability, the ISPR added.Earlier this month, Pakistan and the UK also agreed to strengthensecurity cooperationwhen Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi held delegation-level talks with visiting British Security Minister Dan Jarvis in Islamabad, focusing on counterterrorism, narcotics trafficking, cybercrime and illegal immigration.They also held their annualbilateral dialogueon counter-terrorism in Islamabad, in which they reviewed ongoing bilateral and multilateral counter-terrorism cooperation and reaffirmed their shared commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms.Pakistan and Turkiye, meanwhile, are co-signatories to multiple defence agreements, including theMakkah Defence Pactsigned in August this year with Saudi Arabia, as well as the multilateralBadrdefence cooperation pact in October alongside Qatar and Indonesia.In addition, Pakistan and Turkiye are part of the Regional Four (R4) Group along with Saudi Arabia and Egypt, whichemerged in Marchand has met several times since then.
